5. The aforementioned Bi-lateral treaty existing in between the Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh and the Government of Republic of Korea executed and signed on 10-5-1983, was notified in the Bangladesh gazette on 3-10-1984, with the object to implement the treaty as municipal law for the 'Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to taxes on Income'. This treaty, commonly known as convention, was made pursuant to the power conferred under the provision of section 144(1) of the Income Tax Ordinance 1984 and the Government of Bangladesh has given effect to the said convention in Bangladesh and the same is in force in Bangladesh with the counterpart effected in Korea. 

 2. (i) Further we hereby submit that HECL is a non-resident corporation having its Head Office in Seoul, Korea, and was permitted to work in Bangladesh in the year 2011. There is absolutely nothing showing that HECL has a permanent establishment in Bangladesh and HECL are actually doing business here in this country and that HECL itself are selling products to any person in Bangladesh. That HECL has established an office in Dhaka with the object to collect and despatch information for the Head Office at Seoul, Korea, for smooth transactions between Head Office and the importers in Bangladesh and to enable it to participate in international tenders and to keep nexus between the two countries so that the business activities of HECL be quick and speedy. If any profit is earned by our principal office in Korea under the convention HECL will be taxed in Korea. But HECL cannot be taxed in Bangladesh for its earnings in Korea which is protected under the convention between the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and the Republic of Korea prepared and signed for avoiding of double taxation and also for prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to taxes on income which has the backing of section 144 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 1984 and which is a solemn document entered into between these two Governments. 

 Chapter XVII of the Income Tax Ordinance 1984 containing the provision of section 144 and 145 of the Income Tax Ordinance 1984, as examined elsewhere in this judgment, deals with the affair "Double Taxation Relief". The provision of section 144(1) of the Income Tax Ordinance 1984 provides for executing agreement to avoid double taxation. The provision of section 144(2), containing the Non-obstaritive clause, provides that where such agreement was entered into, the provision of such agreement shall have prevalence against any other law prevailing in Bangladesh. 

 The same 'Non-obstantive clause' was also contained in the earlier provision of section 49 AA of the Income Tax Act 1922 and therefore the provision of section 49AA of the Income Tax Act 1922 had the applicability as against any other law prevailing at the relevant period and therefore it is crystal dear that the provision of the Article of. the convention has a higher status over the provision of any other law of the country including the other provisions of the Income Tax Ordinance 1984. The convention, dated 8 Aunt 1979, as has been Gazette notified on 8 July 1980, has been made through the gateway of the provision of section 144 of the Income Tax-Ordinance 1984 (previously 49AA of the Income T. Act 1922) and, as such, the same has acquired the force of law operating as against the other provision of the Income Tax Act 1922 or the Income Tax Ordinance 1984 in such respect. Therefore, this court finds that the provision of Article-7(3) of the Convention dated 8th August 1979, as annexed with the Gazette notification dated 8th July 1980 has given a privilege to the Assessee-applicant, being covered by the said convention, to get an allowance of the entire administrative expenses of its Permanent Establishment in Bangladesh as an allowable deduction from its profit, under the provision of section 29(xxvii) of the Income Tax Ordinance 1984.
